questions.question: Prior to India, which country introduced Five-Year Plans for policy-making purposes?
questions.questionHtml: Prior to India, which country introduced Five-Year Plans for policy-making purposes?

options.text: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
options.html: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.

Key Points

  • The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) was the first country to introduce the concept of Five-Year Plans.
  • The USSR introduced its first Five-Year Plan in 1928 under the leadership of Joseph Stalin.
  • The primary goal of the first Five-Year Plan was to rapidly industrialize the nation and boost its economy.
  • The success of the Soviet Five-Year Plans influenced many other countries, including India, to adopt similar planning strategies for economic development.

Additional Information

  • Five-Year Plans
    • Five-Year Plans are centralized and integrated national economic programs.
    • The concept was first implemented in the Soviet Union and later adopted by various other countries.
    • These plans aim to develop sectors such as agriculture, industry, and services by setting specific targets over a five-year period.
    • The plans are designed to achieve rapid economic development and are often associated with socialist and centrally planned economies.
  • Soviet Five-Year Plans
    • The first Soviet Five-Year Plan (1928-1932) focused on the rapid industrialization of the USSR, particularly in heavy industries such as steel, coal, and machinery.
    • The plan also aimed to collectivize agriculture to increase productivity and ensure state control over food supplies.
    • Despite initial challenges and resistance, the first plan achieved significant industrial growth and laid the foundation for future economic development.
    • Subsequent Five-Year Plans continued to build on these achievements, with varying degrees of success and challenges.
  • India's Five-Year Plans
    • India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans after gaining independence in 1947.
    • The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to oversee the formulation and implementation of these plans.
    • India's first Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture, irrigation, and energy production to rebuild the economy after independence.
    • India continued to implement Five-Year Plans until the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.solution: The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007) in India aimed at achieving an 8% GDP growth rate, reducing poverty, and improving the quality of life through better education, health, and infrastructure. By the end of this plan, India emerged as one of the fastest-growing economies. The plan set 'monitorable targets' for key development indicators, emphasizing measurable outcomes and accountability.

questions.question: Which of the following five year plan of India was a complete failure?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following five year plan of India was a complete failure?
questions.solution: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed for self-reliance in agriculture and industry but failed due to several factors. It coincided with the Indo-China War (1962) and the Indo-Pakistan War (1965), diverting resources and focus. Additionally, severe droughts in 1965 and 1966 crippled the agricultural sector, leading to significant economic setbacks and unmet targets. The plan's failure contrasts with other plans like the First Five Year Plan (1951-1956), which focused on agriculture and irrigation, and the Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961), which emphasized industrialization.

questions.question: After the first five-year Plan of India, two subsequent five-year plans were formulated till ___
questions.questionHtml: After the first five-year Plan of India, two subsequent five-year plans were formulated till ___
questions.solution: After India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956), which focused on agricultural development and exceeded its growth target, two subsequent Five-Year Plans were formulated until 1965. The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), known as the Mahalanobis Plan, prioritized industrialization and heavy industries. The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) under Indira Gandhi aimed at growth with stability and self-reliance, and included significant events like the nationalization of 14 major banks and the Indo-Pak war of 1971. The Planning Commission, established in 1950, oversaw these plans to promote economic growth.

questions.questionHtml: What was the target growth rate of the first five-year plan in India?
questions.solution: The first Five-Year Plan in India aimed for a target growth rate of 2.1 percent and concluded in March 1956. Initiated in 1951, the plan focused on effective resource utilization, prioritizing agricultural growth and living standards. India implemented a total of 12 Five-Year Plans from 1951 to 2017, each emphasizing various aspects such as industrialization, poverty alleviation, self-reliance, social justice, modernization, liberalization, and sustainable development. These plans collectively shaped India's economic policies and development trajectory over the decades.

questions.solution: India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) on 1 January 1995. questions.question: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
questions.questionHtml: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7.

Key Points

  • India's first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on the agricultural sector.
  • From 1947 to 1990, a total of 7 Five-Year Plans were successfully completed in India.
  • The Five-Year Plans aimed at economic development through various sectors like agriculture, industry, and services.
  • The seventh Five-Year Plan ended in 1990, marking the completion of 7 such plans within the specified period.

Additional Information

  • Five-Year Plans in India
    • The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
    • They were modeled after the Soviet Union's centralized economic planning, aiming to promote rapid industrialization and economic development.
    • Each plan was formulated, executed, and monitored by the Planning Commission of India, which was established in 1950.
    • The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on the agricultural sector, aiming to overcome food shortages and improve living standards.
  • Planning Commission
    • The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
    • It was established in 1950 by a Cabinet resolution under the advice of the first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
    • The Commission was tasked with assessing the country's resources and formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources.
    • In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) by the Narendra Modi government.
  • Objectives of the Five-Year Plans
    • The primary objectives were to increase national income, achieve full employment, reduce inequalities of income and wealth, and establish a socialist pattern of society.
    • Other specific objectives included reducing poverty, improving infrastructure, and enhancing the quality of life for Indian citizens.
  • Significance of the Five-Year Plans
    • The Five-Year Plans were instrumental in transforming India's economy from an agrarian base to a more diversified one with a substantial industrial sector.
    • They laid the foundation for modern economic development and contributed to significant improvements in various economic indicators, such as GDP growth and poverty reduction.
    • The plans also played a critical role in establishing and expanding public sector enterprises and infrastructure development across the country.

questions.question: After independence, India launched its First FYP in 1951, under _________ influence of first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.solution: After independence, India launched its First Five-Year Plan (FYP) in 1951 under the socialist influence of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The plan aimed to develop the agriculture sector, which was crucial to the Indian economy, by focusing on land reforms, irrigation, and infrastructure. Nehru was influenced by the Soviet model of centralized planning, and the plan emphasized a mixed economy with both public and private sectors. Prepared by the Planning Commission of India, it aimed for a 2.1% annual growth rate in national income, laying the foundation for subsequent economic policies and plans.

Key Points

  • The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in 1951.
  • The main focus of the First Five-Year Plan was on the agricultural sector, aiming to increase the output and productivity of the agricultural sector.
  • The overall growth target set for the First Five-Year Plan was approximately 2.1% per annum.
  • This plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which emphasized the importance of investment for economic growth.

Additional Information

  • Five-Year Plans of India
    • The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs, introduced by the Government of India, aimed at achieving rapid economic growth and development.
    • They were inspired by the Soviet model of economic planning and were implemented from 1951 to 2017.
    • Each plan had its specific objectives and priorities, addressing various sectors such as agriculture, industry, education, and health.
    • The Planning Commission, which was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015, was responsible for formulating and monitoring these plans.
  • Harrod-Domar Model
    • The Harrod-Domar model is an economic growth model that suggests that the growth rate of an economy depends on the level of savings and the productivity of investment.
    • According to this model, higher savings and investment rates lead to higher economic growth rates.
    • The model emphasizes the role of capital accumulation in driving economic growth and development.
    • This model was used as a theoretical foundation for the First Five-Year Plan of India.
  • Agricultural Sector in India
    • Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy, being the primary source of livelihood for a significant portion of the population.
    • The First Five-Year Plan aimed to increase agricultural production to achieve food self-sufficiency and improve rural livelihoods.
    • Various initiatives, such as irrigation projects, land reforms, and improved agricultural practices, were undertaken to boost agricultural productivity.

  • The BPL census aimed to identify households living below the poverty line, which would be eligible for various welfare schemes.

Additional Information

  • Below Poverty Line (BPL):

questions.question: During the Fourth Five-Year Plan, the process of nationalisation of banks took place. How many banks were nationalised during this period?
questions.questionHtml: During the Fourth Five-Year Plan, the process of nationalisation of banks took place. How many banks were nationalised during this period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 14.

Key Points

  • The process of nationalisation of banks during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) was a significant move in India's banking history.
  • A total of 14 major commercial banks were nationalised by the Indian government on 19 July 1969.
  • This move aimed to align banking operations with the economic and social goals of the country, ensuring better control over credit delivery.
  • The nationalisation targeted banks with deposits of Rs. 50 crores or more, bringing them under the control of the government.
  • It marked a pivotal step towards the expansion and spread of banking facilities across the rural and semi-urban areas of India.

Additional Information

  • Nationalisation of Banks:
    • Refers to the process where private sector banks are transferred into public ownership by the government.
    • The primary objective was to ensure sufficient credit for agriculture, small industry, and exports, and to promote banking habits among the population.
  • Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974):
    • Focused on growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
    • It aimed at accelerating the process of industrialisation and growth of the agricultural sector.
  • Impact of Nationalisation:
    • Led to significant branch expansion and increased access to banking services in rural and semi-urban areas.
    • Facilitated better implementation of government policies and schemes aimed at poverty alleviation and rural development.
  • Subsequent Nationalisation:
    • A second wave of nationalisation occurred in April 1980, when six more commercial banks were nationalised.
    • This brought the total number of nationalised banks in India to 20.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the government opt for a plan holiday after the seventh five - year plan?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did the government opt for a plan holiday after the seventh five - year plan?
questions.solution: After the completion of the Seventh Five-Year Plan in 1989, India experienced a period known as a plan holiday from 1990 to 1992. This was a strategic pause in the regular Five-Year Plans, which are central to India's economic planning process. The concept of a plan holiday allows the government to reassess its economic strategies & priorities without the constraints of an ongoing plan. During this period, the focus was on stabilizing the Indian economy, which faced severe fiscal and balance of payments crises, leading to the liberalization reforms of 1991.

questions.question: What is the time period of the rolling plan during the five-year plan in India?
questions.questionHtml: What is the time period of the rolling plan during the five-year plan in India?
questions.solution: The rolling plan in India was introduced by the Janata Party government and implemented after the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979). It was operational from 1978 to 1980, focusing on annual review and revision to adapt to changing economic conditions. This flexible approach replaced the rigid five-year framework, allowing for course corrections based on economic performance. The rolling plan was eventually replaced by the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985) when the Congress government returned to power. India's Five-Year Plans, initiated in 1951, aimed at strategic economic development, with the Planning Commission overseeing their formulation and implementation.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following five year plan of India aim was to make India a 'self-reliant' and 'self-generating' economy?
questions.solution: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed to make India a 'self-reliant' and 'self-generating' economy by focusing on agriculture, especially wheat production, and establishing heavy industries to reduce import dependence. Despite facing challenges from the Sino-Indian War (1962) and Indo-Pakistan War (1965), which diverted resources to defense, the plan laid the foundation for future self-reliance policies. It targeted a 5% annual increase in national income and aimed to expand basic industries, transport, and communication. However, due to the wars and economic challenges, many targets were unmet, leading to three annual plans before the Fourth Five Year Plan.

This statement is true as the green revolution was mainly focused on increasing the productivity of high-yielding crops, which required a certain level of investment and resources that small farmers could not afford.
    • The green revolution benefited farmers who had access to land, capital, technology, and know-how. This statement is also true as the green revolution required a certain level of resources and infrastructure to be successful, and farmers who had access to these resources were able to benefit from it.
    • The green revolution led to the displacement of tenant cultivators in many cases. This statement is also true as the green revolution led to the consolidation of landholdings and the displacement of small farmers and tenant cultivators who could not compete with the larger farmers.

questions.question: Which of the following five year plan of India aimed at accelerating food grain production, increasing employment opportunities & raising productivity with focus on 'food, work & productivity'?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following five year plan of India aimed at accelerating food grain production, increasing employment opportunities & raising productivity with focus on 'food, work & productivity'?
questions.solution: The Seventh Five-Year Plan of India (1985-1990) aimed at accelerating food grain production, increasing employment opportunities, and raising productivity with a focus on "food, work, and productivity." Led by the Congress Party under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, it emphasized social justice, modern technology, agricultural development, and anti-poverty programs. The plan targeted a 5.0% growth rate, achieving an actual growth rate of 6.01% and a per capita income growth rate of 3.7%. It aimed to improve industry productivity, self-reliance, and inclusive economic growth, making India an independent economy.

questions.questionHtml: The _______five year plan of India could not take off in 1990 due to the fast changing political situation at the Centre.
questions.solution: The Eighth Five Year Plan of India, which was set to start in 1990, was delayed due to political instability at the Centre. It eventually commenced in 1992 and continued until 1997. The primary aim of the Eighth Plan was the modernization of the industrial sector, with a focus on technical development. The plan successfully carried forward India's industrial and technological advancements. The initial focus of earlier plans included agriculture, industrialization, and poverty elimination, with notable models such as the Harrod-Domar and P.C. Mahalanobis models guiding these strategies.

questions.question: In how many phases did the Indian Economy experience the success of the Green Revolution?
questions.questionHtml: In how many phases did the Indian Economy experience the success of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Two.

Key Points

  • The Green Revolution in India experienced success in two phases:
    • Phase 1 (1967-1972):-
      • Introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds for wheat
      • Increased production of wheat, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh
      • Transformation of India from a food-deficient to a food-sufficient nation 
    • Phase 2 (1972-1984):-
      • Expansion of HYV technology to other crops, such as rice, maize, and millet
      • Wider adoption of HYV seeds across different regions of India
      • Further increase in agricultural production and food security

Additional Information

  • Green Revolution:-
    • It was a period of agricultural modernization that began in the 1960s and transformed agriculture in India.
    • The Green Revolution involved the introduction of new technologies, such as high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides, as well as the expansion of irrigation systems.
    • These technologies led to a dramatic increase in agricultural production, particularly for wheat and rice, and helped to India achieve food self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Which of the following five-year plan of India has achieved its target growth?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following five-year plan of India has achieved its target growth?
questions.solution: The Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997) of India successfully achieved its target growth by focusing on industrial modernization, technological improvement, and infrastructure development. This period saw significant economic liberalization and reforms that promoted private sector participation, leading to increased foreign investments and a market-oriented economy. The plan's target growth rate was 5.6%, but it achieved an average growth rate of 6.8%. In contrast, the Eleventh Plan (2007-2012) targeted 9% but achieved around 8% due to the 2008-2009 global financial crisis, while the Ninth and Tenth Plans also fell short of their growth targets.

questions.question: When were the two annual plans carried out?
questions.questionHtml: When were the two annual plans carried out?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is After the seventh Five-Year Plan.

Key Points

  • The two annual plans were carried out from 1990-1992.
  • These plans were implemented after the completion of the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990).
  • The annual plans were introduced due to the political and economic instability in the country at that time.
  • The Eighth Five-Year Plan could not start in 1990 due to economic crisis and political uncertainties.
  • These annual plans focused on immediate needs and short-term goals rather than long-term planning.

Additional Information

  • Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990)
    • The Seventh Plan aimed at accelerating food production, increasing employment opportunities, and improving productivity.
    • It focused on establishing a self-sufficient economy with robust infrastructure.
    • The plan emphasized policies for poverty alleviation and technological advancement.
    • It achieved significant growth in the agricultural and service sectors.
  • Economic Crisis of 1991
    • India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, leading to the introduction of economic reforms.
    • The crisis necessitated immediate policy measures to stabilize the economy.
    • The reforms included liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG) policies.
    • These measures helped to open up the Indian economy to global markets.
  • Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997)
    • Formulated after the 1991 economic reforms, focusing on human resource development and industrial growth.
    • It aimed to achieve high growth rates and reduce poverty.
    • The plan emphasized the modernization of industries and infrastructure development.
    • It marked a shift from centralized planning to a more market-oriented approach.
  • Significance of Annual Plans
    • Annual plans are short-term plans formulated for one year.
    • They are used during periods of transition between two Five-Year Plans.
    • These plans focus on immediate needs and short-term objectives.
    • They provide flexibility to address unforeseen economic challenges and political instability.
